chapters.title: Phone Number Verification
chapters.subtitle: Know which numbers are real before you call

steps.text: Phone number verification asks an outside service whether a contact's number is real, and what kind of line it is. This video shows why it exists, how to set up a provider, how to read the results, and how to work the queue of checks.

chapters.title: Why verify phone numbers
chapters.subtitle: Stop spending agent time on dead numbers

steps.text: A purchased list, an old import or a form typed in a hurry is full of numbers that do not work. Every call to one of them is time an agent does not get back.
The kind of line matters too. A text sent to a landline is never read, and a mobile number is the one most likely to answer.
Checking each number by hand is not realistic, and the services that do it charge for every check.
Verification checks each number once, automatically, and shows the answer next to the number: valid or not, mobile, landline or VoIP.

chapters.title: When numbers are checked
chapters.subtitle: New, changed, due again, or retried

steps.text: A number is checked when a contact is saved with a new or changed number. The site checks the contact's preferred number: cell first, then home, office, work and other.
A verified number is checked again after the revalidation interval, so a number that stopped working does not stay green forever. A background task looks for due numbers every few minutes.
Someone can also retry a check from the queue. Because the services charge per check, a number is never checked more often than this.
If no provider is set up yet, new numbers wait, and they are checked as soon as a provider is available.

chapters.title: Set up a provider
chapters.subtitle: The service that checks the numbers

steps.text: Open Settings, Phone Number Verifications. The General tab holds the rules that apply to every provider. Until a provider is switched on, the page says that none is enabled.
Each service has its own tab. AbstractAPI needs only an API key from your account.

Twilio asks for an Authentication type: an API key SID and secret, which Twilio recommends for everyday use, or an Account SID and Auth Token, which suits testing. You can also set a Country code for numbers stored without one, and Data packages for extra line information.
On the Veriphone tab, switch on Enable this provider and paste the API key. The key is stored securely, and the box stays empty afterward.
Click Save. The General tab now offers a Default provider. Choose a provider, or First available provider to use the first one that is switched on.

Revalidation interval says how many days a verified number stays verified. Maximum verification attempts is how many failed checks in a row the site accepts before it stops retrying a number by itself.
Request delay is the pause between checks when many numbers are checked in a row. Raise it if the service complains about too many requests. Click Save.

chapters.title: Read the status icons
chapters.subtitle: The answer, next to the number

steps.text: Wherever a phone field shows a checked number, an icon shows the result. Open a contact: a green check means the service confirmed the number. Point at it to see the date of the check.
A red icon means Invalid: the service says the number is not valid. Do not call it, and ask the customer for a new one.
A warning sign means Failed: the check itself did not work, for example because the service was unavailable. The status is unknown, not invalid, and a failed check never marks a number invalid.
A grey question mark means the number has not been checked yet. It is checked shortly after the contact is saved.
Open Tools, Phone Verifications Queue. It lists every number that has verification data, with a tile for each status that adds up to the total.
Each row shows the number, its status, the provider, how many attempts were made, and when the last one was, with the contact it belongs to.
Click the Failed tile. Failed means the last check failed and the site will try again by itself.
Needs attention means the check failed Maximum verification attempts times in a row, so the site stopped trying. The latest error is shown in red, so you can tell a provider outage from a bad number.
Use Search by phone number to find a record, and the sort list to put the most recent or the oldest attempts first.

To check one number again, open its Actions menu and click Verify again. A failed number has a Retry now button instead. The check is queued and runs shortly after. Here the service cannot be reached, so the record shows the error.
Tick several records, then click Retry selected. Retry all failed re-queues every failed and needs-attention record on every page that matches your search.

chapters.title: Read the report
chapters.subtitle: The state of all your numbers

steps.text: Open Reports, General, Phone Number Verifications. Verification status counts the contacts, and the verified, unverified and invalid numbers, the failures, and the success rate.
Line and queue status shows how many numbers are mobile, landline or VoIP, how many are pending, and how many need to be checked again.
Provider usage shows how many records each provider checked, which is useful when you compare what the services cost. The Export CSV button downloads the report as a file.
Before a calling campaign, import the list and let the checks run. Agents then work the verified numbers, and the invalid ones are set aside.
Before a text campaign, check how many numbers are mobile. Those are the ones that can read a text.
Keep the data clean over time. The revalidation interval brings old numbers back for a new check.
Watch the Needs attention tile. A sudden jump usually means the provider key expired or the service is down, and a single Retry all failed fixes it once it is back.
Set up a provider once, and every new number is checked for you. Read the icon next to the number, work the queue, and keep the results fresh. Thanks for watching.
